reason: David explicitly takes accountability for the sin committed. He confesses 'I have sinned greatly' (וַיֹּאמֶר דָּוִיד אֶל־ הָאֱלֹהִים חָטָאתִֽי מְאֹד), acknowledges his foolishness, and most critically, intercedes on behalf of the people: 'these are but sheep, what have they done?' (הֲלֹא אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי לִמְנוֹת בָּעָם וַאֲנִי־ הוּא אֲשֶׁר־ חָטָאתִי וְהָרֵעַ הֲרֵעוֹתִי וְאֵלֶּה הַצֹּאן מֶה עָשׂוּ). He beseeches God to direct judgment toward himself and his house rather than the people. David's response demonstrates clear acceptance of responsibility for his leadership failure and his genuine concern for the welfare of the Hebrew people he governs.
